analysis.title: IG Credit Strategist: Fear > greed
key_insights: BofA expects IG credit spreads to stay weak into year-end on elevated volatility and AI supply concerns. The IG index spread was 89bps as of Oct-29, about 5bps wider in October.

The key question is whether hyperscalers bring large new issue deals in November. The MSFT deal on Thursday and ORCL commentary at its investor day raise the odds of supply versus the weak market in the first half of October.

Spreads offer better value, but BofA says the 'greed' is more than offset by 'fear' of mark-to-market risk. The 20d standard deviation of daily spread moves for the liquid IG index rose from 0.9 in September to 2.0.
Hyperscaler negative free cash flow should mostly go away in 2028, so the supply overhang should ease at some point in 2027. BofA calls AI credit a great buying opportunity then.

Tom Curcuruto estimates hyperscalers need to issue about $320bn in the corporate bond market between now and year-end 2027. BofA's November supply forecast assumes a high chance of hyperscaler supply.

BofA forecasts $175bn of US IG supply in November 2026, the busiest November on record versus $138bn in November 2025 and above a $165bn seasonal baseline. October supply is tracking about $100bn versus a $110bn forecast. Drivers are the post-earnings window for AI and M&A, an October backlog, and 10yr yields about 30bps below the 5.3% October peak.
IG net supply less coupon income should rise from -$10bn in October to +$35bn in November, implying weaker technicals.

IG spreads underperformed other markets in October. Spread widening was led by SPCX (+65bps), ORCL (+43bps) and AVGO (+35bps). AI stocks fell, led by GOOGL (-18%) and META (-14%). IG widened more than rate vol (MOVE 3M down 6pts) and more than US stocks ex. AI (+8% MtD). The HY/IG spread ratio compressed to 3.7 from 3.9 on Oct-14.
Liquidity has worsened. The 10d MA of intraday spread range for the liquid IG index reached 3bps in October from 1bp on Sept-4. Off-the-run bid-ask spreads rose to 2.1bps from 1.6bps.

The higher-quality AI sector has cheapened about 25bps YtD versus the index on a rating and maturity adjusted basis. AI trades 63bps wide to the index and Telecom 35bps wide. Aerospace/Defense is 37bps tight and Food, Bev & Bottling 25bps tight.

2027 IG fundamentals should be stronger. Debt growth for the median IG non-financial issuer ex. Utilities is below 1% YoY in 2026, leverage could fall to about 2015 levels in 2027, and upgrades are steady. Interest coverage could decline as issuers roll out of low-coupon debt. The average IG index coupon should rise about 17bps in 2027.

Consensus calls for S&P 500 EPS growth of 16% in 2027 versus 34% in 2026. Core sectors (ex. Tech, Energy, Financials, Utilities) slow to 7% from 25%, implying IG EBITDA growth of about 5% in 2027 versus 11% in 2026. BofA economists forecast domestic demand growth of +2.6% in 2027 versus +2.7% in 2026.

Hedging Iran escalation risk is getting expensive. Oil is back at March/April highs. Energy trades 16bps rich to the index versus 5bps rich in March, and non-cyclical sectors are at their richest since Nov 2023. BofA still prefers hedges: US issuers over European Yankees, and less cyclical sectors with spread (Insurance, Utilities, Telecom).

The October FOMC was read as dovish, a repeat of July but smaller: the 30yr Treasury yield rose 4bps versus 11bps in July. Chair Warsh did not explain why the Fed did not hike. Market pricing subtracted about 6bps from the policy rate by June 2027 and 5yr5yr breakevens rose. Rates strategists expect a more hawkish Fed and a flatter yield curve eventually, which implies a steeper 5s10s IG spread curve.

Q3 earnings tracking: +23.7% YoY earnings growth and +9.1% revenue growth for US IG issuers. Core issuers (ex. Energy, Finance, Tech/AI) are at +7.0% versus +7.7% in 2Q-26. Earnings are +2.9% above start-of-season expectations (versus +8.2% in 2Q and a +3.7% pre-Covid average). Revenue is +1.8% above (pre-Covid average +0.7%).

Japanese life insurers plan on net to reduce foreign bond allocation in fiscal 2H-2026 (4 of 10 plan to cut hedged foreign bonds, 6 unhedged). They net sold $1.8bn of long-term foreign bonds in September. BofA expects no big change in foreign demand for IG.
AI-related USD bond issuance totals $352bn YtD ($308bn IG, $44bn HY) and $502bn since 2025. Hyperscalers account for $182bn of IG YtD. AI is 4.7% of the IG index and 3.1% of HY.

This week's IG gross supply was $60.0bn versus a $25-40bn estimate, including about $25bn from MSFT. New issue concession rose to 9bps from 7bps. Supply is expected at $30-40bn next week, limited by US elections. Net demand technicals were +$43.1bn this week and are expected at +$9.0bn next week.

Fund flows for the week ending Oct-28: US HG bond funds and ETFs +$4.35bn (versus +$1.22bn), HG ETFs +$7.20bn, HG funds -$2.85bn. Loans saw -$0.31bn, the biggest outflow since March 2026. HY +$1.80bn, the biggest inflow in 3 months. Equities +$14.54bn, money markets -$11.36bn.

Quality and sector positioning: BBB moves to neutral to lower portfolio beta. Overweight Pipelines, Insurance, Utilities and Energy. Underweight tight sectors with re-leveraging and M&A risk (Consumer Products, Health Care, Food/Bev, Retail, Telecom). 10s30s spread curve stays flat and 5s10s should steepen.

earnings_insights: Q3-26 US IG public issuers: aggregate earnings growth +23.7% YoY (BofA tracker, actual where reported, consensus otherwise) and revenue growth +9.1% YoY. 49% of issuers have reported, 56% of expected aggregate earnings.
Core US IG issuers ex. Energy, Finance and Tech/AI: +7.0% YoY earnings growth versus +7.7% in 2Q-26 (tracked, mix of actual and consensus).

Earnings are +2.9% above expectations at the start of the season on Oct 7, versus +8.2% in 2Q-26 and a +3.7% pre-Covid average. Revenue surprise is +1.8% versus +3.1% in 2Q-26 and a +0.7% pre-Covid average.

Sector earnings surprise: Energy +22.6%, Aerospace/Defense +15.1%, Insurance +13.1%. Weakest: Automobiles -7.2%, Health Care -1.0%, AI -0.8%. Weakest YoY earnings growth: Transportation, Insurance, Other. Strongest: Energy (+125%), Technology ex. AI (+68%), AI (+29%).

Spread reaction to earnings has been mixed. Largest tightening after earnings: DOW (-8bps), HAL (-4bps). Largest widening: T (+15bps), GM (+3bps), NFLX (+3bps), BAC (+3bps). ORCL's stock fell 8% relative to the S&P with no spread change.
The results exclude BA, and ignore META's one-time tax charge in 3Q-25 and one-time litigation charge in 3Q-26.

Busiest November on record. Weaker technicals, with risk to the upside.
Volatility suppressed issuance, and some backlog could shift into November.

Earnings growth decelerates but stays decent.

trade_ideas.description: Long US issuers over European Yankee issuers as an Iran escalation hedge
trade_ideas.rationale: Hedges Iran escalation risk when spreads are tight, especially away from AI.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight less cyclical sectors with spread (Insurance, Utilities) and Energy as an Iran hedge
trade_ideas.rationale: These sectors are defensive against an energy shock and still offer spread.
trade_ideas.risk: Energy and non-cyclical sectors are at multi-year tights, so hedging is expensive.

trade_ideas.description: Move BBB positioning to neutral and take down portfolio beta
trade_ideas.rationale: Spreads are weaker and expected to stay wider into year-end 2026.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Pipelines for spread. Underweight Consumer Products and Health Care
trade_ideas.rationale: Pipelines offer more spread, while the other two are tight with elevated re-leveraging and M&A risk.

trade_ideas.description: 5s10s IG spread curve steepener, with 10s30s staying flat
trade_ideas.rationale: A more hawkish Fed and a flatter Treasury curve should steepen 5s10s, and higher yields and less long-end supply support a flat 10s30s.
trade_ideas.risk: 10yr spreads could be hurt by weaker HG fund and ETF flows.

trade_ideas.description: Buy AI hyperscaler credit spreads once supply overhang eases in 2027
trade_ideas.rationale: Hyperscaler negative free cash flow mostly goes away in 2028, so supply eases in 2027 and cheap AI spreads should compress.
trade_ideas.risk: Heavy November supply and GPU funding deals could widen spreads further first.

risk_factors: Heavy hyperscaler and M&A issuance in November, with the risk to the upside of the $175bn forecast.
Iran escalation after the US elections, with oil at the March/April highs and inventories depleted.
GPU funding deals as another supply risk.
Higher mark-to-market spread volatility and worse liquidity, especially in off-the-run bonds.
Weaker HG fund and ETF flows could hurt 10yr spreads.
Interest coverage could decline as issuers roll into higher-coupon debt.
A hawkish Fed, since strong growth and elevated inflation could eventually force hikes.

vol_and_positioning: The 20d standard deviation of daily spread changes for the liquid IG index rose to 2.0bps from 0.9bps in September.
The MOVE 3M index is down 6pts in October while IG spreads are about 5bps wider, so IG underperformed rate vol.
The IG intraday spread range (10d MA) reached 3bps versus 1bp on Sept-4. Off-the-run bid-ask spreads are 2.1bps versus 1.6bps.
Dealer inventories of IG corporate bonds were estimated at -$1.8bn on Oct-29 versus -$7.8bn on Oct-21. Dealers added $7.0bn over the past week.
IG portfolio trading was net selling across all maturities and ratings over the five days ending Oct-29. Client net sales were -$3bn on Oct-29.
The CDS-cash basis is -36bps as of Oct-27.
The share of credit investors concerned about re-leveraging is 7% in the October survey, down from 30% in January.
geopolitical: News reports of a potential Iran escalation after the US elections next week drove oil back to the March/April highs. Inventories are more depleted than in April.
The US elections next week limit issuance opportunities.

tension_points.bull_case: AI spreads are cheap (about 63bps wide to the index), and the IG market can absorb hyperscaler supply over time. Hyperscaler negative FCF mostly goes away in 2028 and supply eases in 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Mark-to-market risk, record November supply and GPU funding deals outweigh the value near term. The fear wins while the supply overhang persists.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Large hyperscaler new issue deals not arriving in November, which would ease the supply overhang.

tension_points.bull_case: Low debt growth (under 1% YoY), steady upgrades and falling leverage point to stronger 2027 credit quality.
tension_points.bear_case: Interest coverage may decline as issuers roll into higher coupons, and technicals weaken on heavy supply.

theme_stances.key_argument: Fear of mark-to-market risk and supply outweighs better spread value while the supply overhang persists in November.
theme_stances.evidence: The fear should continue to win while the supply overhang persists

theme_stances.key_argument: Prefer hedges against a global energy shock because spreads are tight away from AI, even though hedging is costlier.
theme_stances.evidence: we continue to prefer to be hedged against the risk of global energy shock

theme_stances.key_argument: Lackluster borrowing outside M&A and AI means leverage for the typical IG issuer should keep improving in 2027.
theme_stances.evidence: leverage for the typical IG issuer should continue to improve in 2027
